e-562.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
e-562.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) = 4t^2 - 3t^3,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the velocity (in $\textrm m / \textrm s$) of the particle at time $t.$
e-562.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (4{t}^{2}-3{t}^{3})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0) = 2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{3}(0)^{3}-\frac{3}{4}(0)^{4}+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = \dfrac{4}{3}t^3 -\dfrac{3}{4}t^4 + 2.$

e-563.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
e-563.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) =2e^{-t}+6t^2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-4 \,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the speed of the particle at the moment  $t=1\,\textrm{s}.$
e-563.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2{e}^{-t}+6{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2(-{e}^{-t})+\frac{6}{3}{t}^{3}+C \\  & =-2{e}^{-t}+2{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0) = -4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =-2{e}^{-0}+2\cdot {0}^{3}+C \\ -4 & =-2+0+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = -2  e^{-t}+ 2t^3 -2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=1\,\textrm{s}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =-2{e}^{-1}+2(1)^{3}-2 \\  & =-2{e}^{-1}+2-2 \\  & =-\frac{2}{e}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\dfrac 2 e\,\textrm{m/s}.$

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=t^3-t^2-3t+C. Since v(3)=6, 27-9-9+C=6, so C=-3. Therefore option b satisfies both the acceleration and initial velocity.

after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-2t-3$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=6\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-2t-3)\text{d} \\  & ={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(3)=6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =(3)^{3}-(3)^{2}-3(3)+C \\ 6 & =27-9-9+C \\ C & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t-3.$

Question 1

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in ft/s2, given by the function a(t)=3t2−2t−3, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=6ft/s when t=3s, find the velocity (in ft/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=3t2−2t−15
b
 v(t)=t3−t2−3t−3
c
 v(t)=3t3−2t2−3
d
 v(t)=t3−t2−3t−12
e
 v(t)=t3−2t2−t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(3t2−2t−3)d=t3−t2−3t+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(3)=6. Substituting this into the above gives

6=(3)3−(3)2−3(3)+C6=27−9−9+CC=−3.

Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=t3−t2−3t−3.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-2t-3$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=6\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-2t-3)\text{d} \\  & ={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(3)=6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =(3)^{3}-(3)^{2}-3(3)+C \\ 6 & =27-9-9+C \\ C & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t-3.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2t-{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2(1)-(1)^{3}+C \\ 4 & =2-1+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3+2t-{t}^{3}.$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=−5t4+2t+2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=−8m/s when t=0s, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment t=2s.

a
24m/s
b
36m/s
c
 40m/s
d
32m/s
e
48m/s

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration and using v(0)=-8 gives v(t)=-t^5+t^2+2t-8. Hence v(2)=-32+4+4-8=-32 m/s. Speed is |v(2)|=32 m/s, matching option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-5{t}^{4}+2t+2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-8\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-5{t}^{4}+2t+2)\text{d}t \\  & =-{t}^{5}+{t}^{2}+2t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-8.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =-(0)^{5}+(0)^{2}+2(0)+C \\ -8 & =0+C \\ C & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-{t}^{5}+{t}^{2}+2t-8.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =-(2)^{5}+(2)^{2}+2(2)-8 \\  & =-32+4+4-8 \\  & =-32\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $32\,\text{m/s}.$
